controlled_fields.payload.dialogue: may be compressed without changing choices

assumptions: The story is an explicit original adaptation.

payload.premise: A feared Yaksha ordered to guard a sealed rain cistern must choose between its oath and a thirsty child.
payload.theme_question: Is protection still virtuous when it protects ownership instead of life?

character_pressure.CHR001: Wants to remain worthy of an ancient oath but recognizes the oath now serves hoarding.
character_pressure.CHR002: Needs water for her family and refuses to treat the guardian as a mindless monster.

scenes.goal: The child reaches the sealed cistern.
scenes.obstacle: The Yaksha is bound to repel anyone without the owner's mark.
scenes.turn: The child offers the empty cup to the guardian instead of attacking.
scenes.aftermath: The Yaksha sees whom the oath is actually harming.

scenes.goal: The Yaksha decides what it truly guards.
scenes.obstacle: Breaking the seal makes it an oathbreaker and draws the owner's hunters.
scenes.turn: It places its own hand beneath the falling blade and breaks the seal.
scenes.aftermath: Water crosses the forbidden threshold; the Yaksha faces outward as a self-chosen guardian.

beats.action: The child crosses the dry threshold with an empty cup.
beats.information: Water exists, but ownership blocks access.

beats.action: The Yaksha appears and stops one claw-width from the child.
beats.information: It can kill her but chooses to listen.

beats.action: The Yaksha intercepts the hunter's blade with its left forearm and breaks the cistern seal with its right hand.
beats.information: It redefines the oath through an irreversible choice.

beats.action: Water passes around its feet toward the child while it turns to face the hunters.
beats.information: The monster image remains, but its moral position has changed.

dialogue.speaker: CHR002
dialogue.line: 你守的是水，还是他们的锁？

payload.ending_state: The Yaksha loses sanctioned status and gains chosen responsibility.
